query: run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel
title: Run Claude Code agents in parallel | OpenWiz
description: Run two Claude Code sessions in separate Git worktrees and use OpenWiz to plan, track and review their work as separate tickets.
answer: Run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel by opening two terminals in the same Git repository and starting Claude Code with a different `--worktree` name in each. Use OpenWiz to plan separate tickets and track them on GitHub. With the local setup in OpenWiz 0.1.0, you start each builder yourself.

sections.heading: Give each session its own ticket
sections.body: Choose two small tasks that can start from the same commit and touch different files. For example, give one agent the README and ask the other to add a test for existing behavior. Anthropic's [guide to parallel sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows#run-parallel-sessions-with-worktrees) shows how each worktree gives a session a separate checkout and branch.

steps.name: Install OpenWiz and choose this computer
steps.text: Have Python 3.9 or later, Git and the GitHub CLI installed. Sign in to `gh` and Claude Code, then tell Claude Code `Install OpenWiz`. Choose this computer and finish setup using the 0.1.0 install guide in Sources. When the guide asks you to restart Claude Code, start a new session and say `continue the OpenWiz install`.

steps.name: Approve a plan with independent tickets
steps.text: Choose a GitHub repository you can write to, with at least one commit. Ask your setup agent to plan two independent tasks for that repository. Confirm the spec and approve the plan before starting either builder.

steps.name: Start two Claude Code sessions
steps.text: From your project checkout, run `claude --worktree readme-update` in one terminal and `claude --worktree add-tests` in a second. Give each session its own GitHub ticket link and ask it to work only on that ticket's assigned files.

steps.name: Review the work separately
steps.text: Have each session give you its changes and test results for its own ticket and ask it to open a separate pull request. Review each diff and its checks before deciding whether to merge.

faq.question: Will the two agents edit the same working files?
faq.answer: Each named worktree has its own checkout and branch. Assign different files if you want to reduce conflicts when the branches come back together.

faq.question: Do I need CloudRoom for two Claude Code sessions?
faq.answer: You can run both sessions on your own computer. OpenWiz 0.1.0 starts its automatic fleet in CloudRoom, so with the local setup you launch each builder and review each pull request yourself.
